The good news is that the bug shown in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061 seems to be fixed. The bad news:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ed203f1-95cf-4e15-8cc3-16074a07acd7
Yeah that bug is unrelated to the changes made in this PR.

On my end, this PR introduces the bugs shown in the video.
I updated https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061, and it works (on my end).
On your end. On my end the bug is introduced prior to my changes, but I'll test your PR anyway and see if the bug is still present at my editor scale.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f32aac59-de3c-477a-8ffa-46f0ab122442

> 5. How title_minsize is handled
I think this is the main difference and the reason why compact mode causes a bug. See here. Or I just didn't understand something.

Compact mode doesn't "cause a bug" because of my code, it simply hides the sidebar when the project manager is shrunk. The implementation, which targeted Android devices, had some holes in it, like not being able to turn off compact mode - so #122152 adds those options for desktop users and makes compact mode off by default, which is standard behaviour.

> > 5. How title_minsize is handled
> >    I think this is the main difference and the reason why compact mode causes a bug. See here. Or I just didn't understand something.
> 
> Compact mode doesn't "cause a bug" because of my code, it simply hides the sidebar when the project manager is shrunk. The implementation, which targeted Android devices, had some holes in it, like not being able to turn off compact mode - so #122152 adds those options for desktop users and makes compact mode off by default, which is standard behaviour.

Probably, I didn‘t read the whole PR yet. But I don‘t understand this PR‘s min_size behaviour entirely.

I just updated https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061 and fixed some bugs contained in this PR / https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122152. Here a preview:


Thats https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122152:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f67ce4bd-d683-4369-beb5-6ee847a88a48


Also look at the tags. And that's https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/875f0a44-a081-4e84-b723-d5d43f5977a3

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/678dbaac-a40b-46ae-bf2e-ccedd28b48b8

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d32bf07-7800-46f5-b2ea-76abee2e8203


I tested this with the artifacts, so this should work at your end. I recognized that I could reproduce your errors with the artifacts — the existence of which I hadn't known about until now, since I'm quite new here.

I don't list every bug I fixed, since I believe https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061 is complete at all now. We accomplished this together: I added you as co-author, but if you want the changes to get merged in your PR, you can use them, if I'm a co-author there (I am already). Also, if you found some more issues not mentioned until now, I'll be glad to work on this again with you.

> I just updated #122061 and fixed some bugs contained in this PR / #122152. Here a preview:

I'm confused. What bugs are there in #122152?
Yes, you already mentioned me, that's ok.

Look at the videos. Most important points are:
- Tags (now resizing always first)
- Resizing when window is at minsize (resizing perfectly to minsize)
I did some code fixes and adjusting the values for `abs_minsize` and `title_size` a bit to make it even more precise.
Also a bug in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122152, which was located in `resize_project_titles`. You can see the diff. It's about when side bar size is subtracted.
And some optimizations.

Explain the bugs

> Also a bug in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122152, which was located in resize_project_titles. You can see the diff. It's about when side bar size is subtracted.

What happens when the side bar size is subtracted that is a bug?

> Look at the videos. Most important points are:
>
> -  Tags
>
> -  Resizing when window is at minsize

As for the tags, them not laying flat is a design choice, if there are many smaller tags on a project, the control will get very long vertically, which will make scrolling a bit more annoying.

As for the minimum size of the project manager window, I don't allow the project titles to wrap to the `abs_minsize` because of what will happen if tags are added after it has wrapped to that size, either the title will have to wrap to be even smaller, or the sidebar will be pushed beyond the window to make space for the tag -> which looks broken.

Having the title stop shrinking after a certain point ensures if tags are added at that point, the title will wrap and the sidebar will remain unaffected. It is not a bug, it is a design choice, by initial numbers -> 200 minsize & 800 title size were not chosen out of thin air like your making it seem with statements like these:
> This is fixed through some code fixes and the very accurate testing of the best values for abs_minsize and title_size.

You can go and read through the entire original PR #119580 and look at the commits to see the iteration process yourself. What you are calling bugs are not bugs, you did find a bug, but that bug has been fixed, none of my PRs, not this one or #122152 have introduced any new bugs, the behaviour of my original PR has remained the same, the minimum size thing is the result of #121387, if you believe it to be a bug that the project manager can suddenly shrink way beyond what I allow my titles to wrap to, you'll have to take that up with syntaxerror247.

> As for the tags, them not laying flat is a design choice, if there are many smaller tags on a project, the control will get very long vertically, which will make scrolling a bit more annoying.

Implemented again.

> if you believe it to be a bug that the project manager can suddenly shrink way beyond what I allow my titles to wrap to, you'll have to take that up with syntaxerror247.

No, I don't believe that's a bug. But it isn't that practical too. I would recommand to leave the window minsize as it is now, wich is smaller than your project titles allow.
That's ok.

I implemented the abs_minsize again, so tags won't take too much space. If 200 is too low, you could suggest a more appropriate value.

Your title_size value is very precisely. A bit more precisely is 798, so that's no big difference.

The abs_title_minsize provokes that tags take **less** space than in this PR, not always at least the max tag size.

What exactly don't you like about the new behaviour?

The only issues I had were the tags laying flat and the title shrinking to the `abs_minsize` without tags, which I previously stated would "break" the project manager when a tag is added. Once those issues are addressed, there is no problem with your PR, other than the fact it tries to include the compact mode setting. That really needs to be made its own PR.

> Having the title stop shrinking after a certain point ensures if tags are added at that point, the title will wrap and the sidebar will remain unaffected. It is not a bug, it is a design choice, by initial numbers -> 200 minsize & 800 title size were not chosen out of thin air like your making it seem with statements like these:
> > This is fixed through some code fixes and the very accurate testing of the best values for abs_minsize and title_size.

I meant that I measured pixels and this should be more precise. you said yourself that this value may be adjusted. My wording was not very good., sorry for that, I meant well.

> The only issues I had were the tags laying flat and the title shrinking to the `abs_minsize` without tags, which I previously stated would "break" the project manager when a tag is added. Once those issues are addressed, there is no problem with your PR, other than the fact it tries to include the compact mode setting. That really needs to be made its own PR.

We could use your PR for compact mode. I'll make a suggestion for the fix I made there.

> The only issues I had were the tags laying flat and the title shrinking to the abs_minsize without tags, which I previously stated would "break" the project manager when a tag is added.

Yould cou please add an image or video so I see what you mean?

>I meant that I measured pixels and this should be more precise. you said yourself that this value may be adjusted. My wording was not very good., sorry for that, I meant well.

No, I know what you meant, but like I said, that phrasing makes it seem like I also didn't measure pixels, which I did. I did a lot of iteration on that PR before it was merge ready. The only reason it made it into 4.7.1 was because of this issue #120797.

> Could you please add an image or video so I see what you mean?

The tags laying flat is in your very own video. Also, if you look at where the text wraps in the video of my PR, vs in the video of your PR, you can clearly see the title wraps more in your PR. I wasn't sure if it could wrap more than that if a tag was added then and there, which is why I phrased it like this:
> I don't allow the project titles to wrap to the abs_minsize because of what will happen if tags are added after it has wrapped to that size, either the title will have to wrap to be even smaller, or the sidebar will be pushed beyond the window to make space for the tag -> which looks broken.

> either the title will have to wrap to be even smaller,

Would apply if it could wrap more, wheras:
> or the sidebar will be pushed beyond the window to make space for the tag -> which looks broken.

Would apply if it couldn't.

> or the sidebar will be pushed beyond the window to make space for the tag -> which looks broken.

I saw no other way than pushing the sidbar out of the window, when the window gets too small, like your solution does.

> Would apply if it couldn't.

Did you mean the image?
I guess, allowing to resize the window so small that even for the side bar is not enough space is the best way to get out the maximum of flexibility.

> I saw no other way than pushing the sidbar out of the window, when the window gets too small, like your solution does.

That's the only viable solution when the user is actively shrinking the window, when they've stopped shrinking the window, adding a tag shouldn't move any element out of the view of the window is where the problem would be. I can't say if your implementation did move the sidebar or shrunk the title even more as all I checked at the time was the videos.

> Did you mean the image?

No I meant the quoted statement above it. Also for context, i was refering to the behaviours in the videos in this [comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122095#issuecomment-5219932367)

> I guess, allowing to resize the window so small that even for the side bar is not enough space is the best way to get out the maximum of flexibility

It was changed to be more usebable on Android. You can take a stab at having a different minum size based on whether the device is andriod or desktop, but that will definitely, 100 percent need to be a different PR. And the justification will have to come from the changes made in #121387, so it will in no way be related to this, nor #122061 nor #122152

> It was changed to be more usebable on Android. You can take a stab at having a different minum size based on whether the device is andriod or desktop, but that will definitely, 100 percent need to be a different PR. And the justification will have to come from the changes made in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121387, so it will in no way be related to this, nor https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061 nor https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122152

Due to the sidebar, I find the ability to resize the window smaller than the sidebar very useful. I would leave this on any device, but this is no topic for here.
Thanks!
